disclaimer.title: ~ The disclaimer ~
disclaimer.acknowledge: I will not disconnect the usb cable before instructed to do so
disclaimer.warning: I have downloaded Vacuula from github.com/vacuula, as other sources could contain nefarious modifications
disclaimer.bullet2: If your robot is rainbowing, get in touch!
disclaimer.bullet3: You will need an usb data cable
disclaimer.bullet4: Vacuula is not affiliated with Neato
disclaimer.bullet5: Vacuula modifies your robot software. It does so for the sole reason of allowing your vacuula server to control it. All code; installer, server and scripts are open source, take a look!
disclaimer.bullet6: Make sure your robot is fully charged and connected to the charger!
disclaimer.bullet7: If you have previously done a ESP32-mod you have to remove the device prior of installing Vacuula
disclaimer.bullet8: You proceed on your own risk
serversearch.title: Vacuula needs a server
serversearch.body: Before biting your robot a server needs to be setup. Follow instructions here if not done already
serversearch.detailinfo: 🛈 The server needs to be accessible on both the network the robot will be connected to and on the network controlling devices will be - if separate
serversearch.manual.not_found: No server found at this address
error.title: An error occurred
error.multiple_robots: Multiple robots detected, please only connect one
error.multiple_robots.detailed: Currently the installer only supports one robot at a time, future versions might support selecting amongst the connected.
error.robot_disconnected.detailed: The robot was disconnected during the installation process, please reconnect and try again
error.generic.connect: Failed to connect to the robot
error.generic.upload: Failed to upload Vacuula to robot
error.generic.help: 🛈 Make sure the robot is powered on and connected to your computer via USB. If the problem persists, try restarting the installer and the robot. If it refuses to work, ask for help in the discord!
error.firmware.help: 🛈 Follow the guide on github on how to update your robot to an supported firmware version or ask for help on the discord.
error.gen2.unsupported: Botvac Connected is not yet supported
error.gen2.unsupported.detailed: Unfortunately Vacuula does not yet support the second generation Botvac Connected, but in due time we might manage to add support for it as well! Please get in touch so we can gauge interest between features people want!
connect.title: Connect a robot to your computer with a USB cable
connect.howto: 🛈 There is a USB contact under the dustbin, the green "cable" in the illustration ends at its approximate location
wifi.title: Connect your robot to WiFi
wifi.explanation: Vacuula needs to reach your server!
wifi.ssid.title: Name of wifi network (SSID)
wifi.ssid.gen23.title: Select from available networks
wifi.pass.title: Password, can be blank
wifi.disclaimer: 🛈 Note that the Neato devices supported by Vacuula do not support WPA3, make sure your network uses WPA2 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode. It is also advisable to connect the robot to 2.4GHz if available
wifi.gen23.pre.title: Connect to the robot's WiFi
wifi.gen23.pre.explanation: Connect to WiFi network "Neato-{mac}" on this computer
wifi.gen23.pre.disclaimer: Just like the original app, the Gen2/Gen3 robots need a setup via their own WiFi connection. The installer has automatically reset the network settings on the robot, so the robot wifi should show up soon! It may take up to a couple minutes, if you don't see it even after rescanning, try restarting the installer, the robot or reset network settings manually.
wifi.gen23.explanation.title: Your computer needs to connect to your robots WiFi for the installation procedure
wifi.gen23.explanation.body: Please switch your computers WiFi connection to "{robot-wifi-ssid}". This is only needed during installation
wifi.gen23.disclaimer: 🛈 Only networks visible to the robot can be selected. The Neato devices supported by Vacuula do not support WPA3, make sure your network uses WPA2 or WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode. It is also advisable to connect the robot to 2.4GHz if available
firmware.scan: Checking if your robot's firmware is up-to-date
firmware.title: Firmware update
firmware.subtitle: Vacuula supports the latest versions of the Neato firmware, this is what has been tested and is known to work. Here we will help you update to an supported version!
firmware.install.step.awaiting_ack: Waiting for robot to acknowledge received firmware
firmware.install.step.done.gen3: Uploaded to robot, unfortunately we cannot verify at this stage if it worked, but if it did, the robot should reboot within 30 seconds (we will detect that), and then you can rerun the installer to continue the installation of Vacuula
firmware.install.step.done.gen4: Uploaded to robot, it will continue flashing yellow, this means it is working. It may take up to 15-20 minutes. Keep the robot connected. Let it finish, the robot will automatically reboot when ready and then you can continue with the installation of Vacuula
firmware.install.done.disconnected.gen3: Robot disconnected after firmware update, that most likely means the update was successful
Please wait for the robot to reboot, the red error light will start flashing (as the dustbin is not in place), and then you can click below to restart the installation with supported firmware!
firmware.install.done.disconnected.gen4: Robot disconnected after firmware update, that most likely means the update was successful
Please wait for the robot to reboot, it will do a rainbow of colours, play a sound and then show battery status and white buttons. Once that happens you can click below to restart the installation with supported firmware!
firmware.gen3.factory_reset_ack: For the firmware update to be a guaranteed success, your robot needs to be factory reset. Please confirm that you have done so recently, or see below instructions.
firmware.gen3.factory_reset.explanation: Factory reset your Neato to garentee a successful update. Saying on this page will guide you though the process, do not disconnect the robot. Do the following to reset:
firmware.gen3.factory_reset.instructions:
1. Remove dustbin (blue dot shows powerbutton) 
 2. Press in the two bumper switches as the red arrows show 
 3. Hold down powerbutton until robot turns off, 10s 
 4. Release ONLY the powerbutton when lights are off 
 5. Press powerbutton once (while holding bumper switches) 
 6. Only release bumper when blue light stops flashing
firmware.gen3.factory_reset.disconnected: You are making progress! Robot disconnected, continue holding bumper switches and press powerbutton once!

When you have pressed the powerbutton the robot will start flashing with a blue light, you may release the bumper when the blue light stops. When the robot is fully started (red error will flash because of no dustbin), click below to restart the installer and flash the latest firmware!
firmware.gen3.factory_reset.restart: Once started, click here to restart installer and install latest firmware
firmware.gen3-4.5.3.description: The latest firmware publicly released by Neato. This is the recommended version for Vacuula.
firmware.gen3-4.6.0.description: If your robot is having lidar issues, this firmware was made by Neato for robots brought in for repair. Only choose this one if you are having problems with the lidar, from our testing and analysis it is pretty much identical to 4.5.3.
firmware.gen4-1.7.0.description: The latest firmware publicly released by Neato. This is the recommended version for Vacuula.
provision.title: Setting up your robot
provision.gen4.instructions: To connect to the server, hold down the power button until your robot turns off and wait a few seconds. Then restart the robot and wait until is has fully booted up.
finished.title: Robot bitten by Vacuula
finished.subtitle: You may now disconnect the robot from your computer and turn the robot on! Then please wait for the robot to show up in your Vacuula server!
